reason: The quote is verbatim correct (AirdropSpawnGoal.java:105-109) and Location#distanceSquared really does throw on mismatched worlds (paper-api 1.21.4 bytecode: `if_acmpeq` on getWorld(), message 'Cannot measure distance between ...'), but the stated failure is unreachable because a dropper that leaves the arena world does not keep this goal. In Paper 1.21.4 Entity.teleport(T) branches on the level dimension key and, when it differs, calls teleportCrossDimension, which builds a replacement via EntityType.create(..., DIMENSION_TRAVEL), copies only NBT (restoreFrom -> saveWithoutId/load), and calls removeAfterChangingDimensions() on the old entity; Mob.addAdditionalSaveData serialises no goal data, so the replacement Phantom only has its vanilla registerGoals() set, and this plugin attaches AirdropSpawnGoal exactly once at spawn (WaveManager.java:696-702, the only addGoal site for flying-droppers). The old NMS entity is removed by that same call, and ServerLevel's entity-tick consumer returns on isRemoved() before GoalSelector.tick is reached, so shouldStayActive() is never evaluated with a foreign-world Location. The finding's Goal-API premise is also wrong: GoalSelector.tick invokes WrappedGoal.canContinueToUse() (PaperCustomGoal.canContinueToUse -> handle.shouldStayActive()) only inside `if (isRunning())`; for a goal that is not running only canUse() -> shouldActivate() runs, and shouldActivate() never reads dropper.getLocation() (its player loop is world-guarded at AirdropSpawnGoal.java:173). The DropperAttackGoal:191 guard it cites protects a Player target, and players do keep instance identity across dimensions, so that guard is not evidence for the dropper case; what actually survives as a real (different) issue is that the cross-world replacement silently loses the plugin's custom AI, which is out of scope for F2.
